ON THE 20 th OF JUNE, 2023  MISC. CRIMINAL CASE No. 21804 of 2023  BETWEEN:-
 MANISH MARSKOLE S/O SHRI HEMANT MARSKOLE,
 AGED ABOUT 26 YEARS, OCCUPATION: HOUSEKEEPING  WORK HOTEL MANAGEMENT AT SURAT GUJRA, R/O  VILLAGE MOHARIYA POST, POLICE STATION AND  TEHSIL JUNNARDEV, DISTRICT CHHINDWARA  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RAHUL TRIPATHI - ADVOCATE)
 AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH POLICE  STATION PARASIYA DISTRICT CHHINDWARA  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SMT. RANJANA AGNIHOTRI - DY. GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:

ORDER This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.96/2023 dated 16.4.2023 registered at Police Station Parasiya, District Chhindwara for the offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n) and 506 of IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
He further submits that prosecutrix is a consenting party.
He also submits that prosecutrix is a major lady and she is aged about 23 years.
Applicant does not have any criminal past.
The applicant is in custody since 30.03.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.

He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no Manish Marskole vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85012335/
1 likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.

sentences.text: He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Hon'ble Court.
Upon these grounds, the applicant may be released on bail.
Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
In this case, the prosecutrix was aged about 23 years at the time of incident.
Her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. suggests that she consensually had physical relationship with the applicant.
It appears that the applicant refused to marry and hence she lodged the FIR.

Looking to the fact that in legal perspective, every breach of promise to marry cannot be considered as rape, and also looking to the fact that prosecutrix had relationship for more than a year with the applicant, I find it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE Nitesh Manish Marskole vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85012335/
